meta.title: Routing strategy: buy, partner or build RouteSprout
meta.subtitle: Recommendation for the March 2027 board meeting
meta.purpose: Decide whether to buy RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data; every company and number is fictional

inputs.label: Briefing pack (evidence/briefing-pack.md)
inputs.content: Atlas FieldOps acquisition or partnership briefing pack, sections 1–7

storyline.governing_thought: Partner with RouteSprout in 2027 instead of buying it on the proposed terms, and keep a staged, ARR-priced purchase that diligence must earn

exec_summary.text: The proposed $18M all-cash deal breaks the cash floor and pays back only on the sellers' assumptions

sub_points.text: Price plus integration leaves $2M of cash, $7M below the floor
It covers its costs only if cross-sell reaches $2.3M, 96% of an unsigned plan

exec_summary.text: RouteSprout's customers are less stable than the pitch assumes, so integration must protect renewals

sub_points.text: Logo churn rose from 12% to 21%, and 41 accounts hold 58% of ARR
A full migration uses the whole $4M integration cap, with 30% unscoped

exec_summary.text: Of the four paths, only the partnership meets the board's cash, timing and continuity tests in 2027

sub_points.text: The staged deal clears the floor at signing, then falls below it within a year
The partnership costs a $1.2M minimum and delivers routing this summer

exec_summary.text: Keep buying as an option: run diligence alongside the partnership, then buy only on staged terms

sub_points.text: Upfront cash must stay below about $8.4M, about 1.8 times ARR
The board decides at a Q4 2027 gate; if diligence fails, the partnership continues

next_steps.action: Approve the RouteSprout partnership as Atlas's single 2027 routing strategy and fund preliminary due diligence
Sign API partnership terms with change-of-control protection and roadmap sharing limited to the API scope
Commission the quality-of-earnings review, churn cohort, pipeline check and integration audit
Secure retention commitments from RouteSprout's key engineers and account managers before any offer
Bring a go / no-go on staged, ARR-priced terms within the cash limits, for closing in 2028

constraints.item: Board cash floor of $9.0M at all times; initial spend capped at $15.0M; no financing
constraints.effect: rules out Path A outright and shows the staged deal breaching the floor within a year of losses

constraints.item: One-time integration spend under $4.0M through 2028, with 30% of the work unscoped
constraints.effect: the full migration has no room left; if integration-era support counts, even the staged plan reaches $4.35M; API-first scope is a deal term
deducted from the cash available for a later purchase

constraints.item: Integration-era customer success of $0.85M a year and RouteSprout's continuing −$1.0M EBITDA
constraints.effect: included in every contribution and cash figure; turns the base case into a near-zero contribution

constraints.item: Uptime service credits and renewal risk from a missed 99.7% target (not quantified)
constraints.effect: would lower the acquisition's contribution further; the slides say the figures are before these credits

constraints.item: Only one major routing strategy in 2027
constraints.effect: the partnership is the 2027 strategy; a purchase of the same partner is decided at the Q4 gate and closes in 2028

constraints.item: Earnout of up to $7.0M due in 2029 after renewal tests
constraints.effect: earnout must be payable only from cash above the floor

constraints.item: Build displaces a compliance upgrade with an unestimated customer cost
constraints.effect: would make the build worse than the $0.64M contribution shows; stated on the build slide

alternatives.option: Sign the staged deal (Path B) now, since $14.5M fits under the $15.0M limit
alternatives.why: clears the floor by only $0.5M; a year of losses and support ($1.85M) takes cash below it, and economics are the same near-zero base case

alternatives.option: Build routing in-house for $3.4M and keep all the gross profit
alternatives.why: launches late 2028 at best, adds about $0.64M a year, pays back in about 5.3 years after launch and displaces compliance work

alternatives.option: A restructured staged purchase with a lower upfront payment
alternatives.why: kept as the conditional option after diligence: upfront below about $8.4M once the partnership minimum is paid, earnout tied to retention

alternatives.option: Partner only, with no purchase path
alternatives.why: the founders want to sell and the API is nonexclusive, so the partnership needs change-of-control protection; the purchase option guards against losing the product

failure_threshold.driver: signed cross-sell ARR (and verified ARR) found in diligence
failure_threshold.threshold: the acquisition covers its own costs only at about $2.3M of cross-sell ARR; with signed pipeline near that level, verified ARR and upfront below about $8.4M, buying becomes attractive
failure_threshold.range: acquisition contribution a year: low −$1.21M (finance) / base +$0.07M (Sales VP) / high +$1.4M (sellers' framing)

consistency.headline: Partner with RouteSprout in 2027 instead of buying it on the proposed terms, and keep a staged, ARR-priced purchase that diligence must earn
consistency.fix: Recommendation is 'partner now, buy only conditionally'; no title claims the deal pays back

sidebar.header: No retention uplift belongs in the deal value
bullets: **Routing users:** mostly larger, multi-branch companies with dedicated customer-success teams
**Smaller customers without routing:** differ in size and support as well as in the feature, so the gap does not isolate routing
**What drives renewal:** customer-success interviews point to account managers, not routing features alone
sidebar.implication: Value the deal without a retention uplift, and keep account managers in place through any integration

footnotes: The sales deck concludes "routing causes retention"; the comparison does not control for customer size or support model

lead_message.text: An API-first link protects renewals better than a six-month full migration that uses the whole $4M integration cap

body.assumptions_header: The build is slower and riskier than the partnership on four counts
assumptions: Engineers need at least 18 months for a basic product, so launch comes no earlier than late 2028; a partner could ship a limited offer this summer
At $0.64M a year, the $3.4M build takes about 5.3 years after launch to pay back, a best case given the late launch
The effort displaces a planned compliance upgrade, whose delay has a customer cost not yet estimated
Only one major routing strategy is allowed in 2027, so building rules out the partnership for the year
